sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: Traffic rules are fundamental to maintaining order and safety on increasingly congested urban roads. They regulate speed, lane discipline, signaling, and right-of-way, minimizing accidents and fatalities. Beyond physical safety, adherence fosters social responsibility, civic discipline, and respect for law. Yet, in many regions, enforcement is inconsistent due to inadequate monitoring, corruption, and public apathy. Technological interventions such as surveillance cameras, automated fines, and intelligent traffic management systems have improved compliance but cannot replace societal awareness. Road design, urban planning, and driver education significantly influence effectiveness. Public campaigns emphasizing behavioral change, rather than punitive measures alone, have shown measurable success in some cities. Consequently, traffic regulation represents a dynamic interplay between legal frameworks, infrastructure, technology, and citizen engagement, where rules are necessary but insufficient without collective responsibility.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: The advent of CRISPR-Cas9 and advanced biomedicines marks a watershed moment in human history, offering the god-like power to edit the genetic code itself. We stand on the precipice of eradicating hereditary diseases like cystic fibrosis and sickle cell anemia. However, this scientific velocity outpaces our ethical frameworks. The prospect of “designer babies,” where genetic editing extends beyond therapy to enhancement (intelligence, physical traits), threatens to bifurcate humanity into biological castes. Furthermore, the exorbitant cost of personalized immunotherapies creates a chasm of inequality; biomedicine risks becoming a luxury good rather than a universal right. Unless regulatory bodies enforce equitable access and strict ethical boundaries, biotechnology could paradoxically exacerbate the human suffering it aims to alleviate by entrenching socio-economic disparities at a cellular level.

questions.q: The passage primarily portrays traffic rules as
opts: essential for safety and civic responsibility
questions.why: First three sentences. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Welfare Officer), Feb 2026.

questions.q: Which factor is NOT cited as influencing compliance with traffic rules?
questions.why: Weather is never mentioned. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Welfare Officer), Feb 2026.

questions.q: The author suggests that technological interventions
opts: improve compliance but are insufficient alone
questions.why: They “cannot replace societal awareness”. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Welfare Officer), Feb 2026.

questions.q: What role do public campaigns play according to the passage?
opts: They promote behavioural change with measurable success
questions.why: Seventh sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Welfare Officer), Feb 2026.

questions.q: The tone of the passage can best be described as
questions.why: It analyses causes and points to what works. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Welfare Officer), Feb 2026.

questions.q: The phrase “bifurcate humanity into biological castes” suggests
opts: a split between healthy and sick
a divide between the genetically enhanced wealthy and the unedited poor
a split between humans and AI
questions.why: Enhancement for those who can pay creates two biological classes. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Officer), Mar 2026.

questions.q: What is the “watershed moment” mentioned in the passage?
opts: the development of gene-editing technologies like CRISPR
questions.why: First sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Officer), Mar 2026.

questions.q: The author’s attitude towards biotechnology is
opts: cautiously hopeful but deeply concerned about ethics and equity
questions.why: Hope of curing disease, weighed against ethics and cost. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Officer), Mar 2026.

questions.q: Which is NOT mentioned as a risk of biomedicine?
questions.why: Weapons are never mentioned. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Officer), Mar 2026.

questions.q: What does the “chasm of inequality” refer to?
opts: the gap in access to advanced treatments due to high cost
questions.why: Caused by “the exorbitant cost of personalized immunotherapies”. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Officer), Mar 2026.

questions.q: Identify the error: “One of my friends have gone abroad.”
questions.why: 'One of' takes a singular verb: 'has gone'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct preposition: “She has been suffering ____ fever since Monday.”
questions.why: Suffer from an illness. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Change into passive voice: “Who wrote this letter?”
opts: By whom was this letter written?
By whom this letter was written?
Whom was this letter written by him?
questions.why: 'Who' becomes 'By whom' + was + past participle. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “ubiquitous”:
questions.why: Ubiquitous means present everywhere. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “to turn a blind eye”:
questions.why: Standard idiom. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: President Droupadi Murmu attended the first convocation of AIIMS Bilaspur on 6 October 2026. This AIIMS is in:
questions.why: Bilaspur, Himachal Pradesh. Oct 2026.

questions.q: A National Coach Accreditation Board was announced in 2026 on the recommendation of a task force led by:
Sujeet Kalkal won the men's 65 kg gold at the 2026 Asian Games in:
questions.why: He came back from 2–9 down in the final.

questions.q: United Nations Day and World Polio Day are both observed on:
questions.why: The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945.

questions.q: Goa AI Mission 2027 plans to build a large language model in:
questions.why: Launched in July 2025.

questions.q: Which force launched its first 12-week Women Commando Conversion Course in 2026?
In 2026 India signed Terms of Reference for a preferential trade agreement with SACU, the:
The Global Dryland Congress 2026 was held in:
Hansraj Singh Verma was named India's next Ambassador to:
The Gateway of India in Mumbai commemorates the 1911 visit of:
opts: King George V and Queen Mary
questions.why: Completed in 1924.

questions.q: How many seconds will a 500 m long train take to cross a man walking at 3 km/h in the same direction, if the train's speed is 63 km/h?
questions.why: Relative speed 60 km/h = 50/3 m/s; 500 ÷ 50/3 = 30 s. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: An investor splits money between Stock A (8% dividend) and Stock B (12% dividend), total face value ₹15,000. If the amounts are switched, annual income rises by ₹120. What was the original annual income?
questions.why: Income = 1800 − 0.04x; switched = 1200 + 0.04x. Difference 120 gives x = 9000, so 1800 − 360 = 1440. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: The product of the present ages of a mother and daughter is 1200. Fifteen years ago, the mother's age was 9 times the daughter's. What is the mother's present age?
questions.why: 60 × 20 = 1200, and 45 = 9 × 5. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: Four colleagues X, Y, Z, W have ages in arithmetic progression with common difference 4 years, youngest to oldest. The sum of their ages is 100 years. What is Z's age?
questions.why: 4X + 24 = 100, so X = 19; ages 19, 23, 27, 31. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: Ten years ago the average age of a family of 4 was 18 years. Twins were born since then, and today the average age of the family is 20 years. What is the twins' present age?
questions.why: Adults now 72 + 40 = 112; family of 6 totals 120, so twins sum 8: 4 years each. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: Which pair of numbers comes next? 84 78 72 66 60 54 48
questions.why: Subtract 6 each time. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2024.

questions.q: MAD : JXA :: RUN : ?
questions.why: Each letter moves back 3: R→O, U→R, N→K. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2024.

questions.q: People speculate when they assume something to be true on inconclusive evidence. Which is the best example of speculation?
opts: Francine wears jeans on Friday after reading about 'Casual Fridays' in her employee handbook
Mary sits in traffic and wishes she had taken the train
After consulting guidebooks and her travel agent, Jennifer is confident her hotel is first-rate
When Emily opens the door in tears, Theo guesses she has had a death in the family
questions.why: Only Theo concludes from thin evidence. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2024.

questions.q: Ten new TV shows appeared in September: five sitcoms, three hour-long dramas and two news-magazine shows. By January only seven were still on air, five of them sitcoms. Which statement must be true?
opts: Only one of the news-magazine shows remained on air
Only one of the hour-long dramas remained on air
At least one of the cancelled shows was an hour-long drama
Viewers prefer sitcoms over hour-long dramas
questions.why: Three cancelled shows came from the five non-sitcoms; only two are news shows, so at least one drama went. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2024.

questions.q: Four of the following are alike in an alphabet pattern. Which one does not fit?
questions.why: 1st and 2nd letters are opposites (sum 27) and 3rd = 2nd + 3. MNP: P is N + 2. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2024.

questions.q: Warts and fig-warts, catarrhal discharges and a tendency to overgrowths are clinical features of which miasm?
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Sycosis: infiltration and overgrowth (warts, condylomata).

questions.q: The fundamental cause of most chronic diseases, according to Hahnemann, is:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Psora, sycosis or syphilis.

questions.q: In homoeopathic case taking, a 'concomitant' symptom is one that:
opts: accompanies the chief complaint but has no obvious pathological link to it
is common to all patients with the disease
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Concomitants often individualise the case.

questions.q: A child who is obstinate, slow, sweats on the head, craves eggs and indigestible things, and is afraid of the dark and of dogs, needs:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Calc carb: fearful, slow, eggs.

questions.q: Lack of self-confidence with a domineering manner at home, flatulence, right-sided complaints and aggravation from 4 to 8 p.m. indicate:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Lycopodium: 4–8 p.m.

questions.q: Acute nephritis or dropsy with oedema, scanty urine and thirstlessness, with stinging pains, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Apis: oedema, thirstless.

questions.q: Haemorrhage of dark, thin blood that will not clot, from any orifice, with septic states suggests:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Crotalus: dark, non-clotting blood.

questions.q: The source of the remedy Sepia is:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. An animal source.

questions.q: In the Korsakovian method of potentisation:
opts: the same vial is used throughout, emptied and refilled with fresh vehicle at each step
a new vial is used for each potency
potencies are made only by trituration
the dilution is 1 in 50,000 at each step
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Korsakov's single-vial method; Hahnemannian uses a fresh vial for each step.

questions.q: Which of these is a purposive repertory dealing with a single region?
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Covers diseases of the eye.

questions.q: When two rubrics overlap, one large and one small, the repertoriser usually prefers:
opts: the smaller, more characteristic rubric if it truly fits the patient
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Smaller rubrics are more individualising, but only if accurate.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of POSITIVE feedback?
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Rising oestrogen triggers more LH; most hormones work by negative feedback.

questions.q: The 'fight or flight' response is mediated by the:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Adrenaline and noradrenaline.

questions.q: Amyloidosis is the extracellular deposition of:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Stains with Congo red.

questions.q: The 'Tzanck smear' showing multinucleated giant cells is used to diagnose:
opts: herpes virus infections such as chickenpox
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. A bedside test.

questions.q: Pain and swelling of the parotid glands with fever in a child suggest:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. May cause orchitis after puberty.

questions.q: Tonsillitis that begins on the left side and moves to the right, worse after sleep and from hot drinks, with intolerance of anything around the neck, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Lachesis: left to right, worse after sleep. Lycopodium goes right to left.

questions.q: Hepatitis with jaundice, a yellow-coated tongue taking imprint of teeth, foul breath and night sweats in a mercurial constitution suggest:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Mercurius: imprints of teeth, offensive breath and sweat.

questions.q: The most reliable early sign of pregnancy detected by a urine test is the presence of:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Human chorionic gonadotropin.

questions.q: Signs of dehydration in a child with diarrhoea include sunken eyes, thirst and:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Skin pinch goes back slowly.

questions.q: Cellulitis is:
opts: a diffuse spreading infection of subcutaneous tissue
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Usually streptococcal.

questions.q: The best emergency treatment for a chemical splash in the eye is:
opts: immediate copious irrigation with clean water
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Irrigate for at least 15–20 minutes.

questions.q: The Pulse Polio campaign aims to give oral polio drops to children under:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. On National Immunisation Days.

questions.q: Algor mortis means:
opts: cooling of the body after death
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Used to estimate time since death.

questions.q: The term 'patient autonomy' means:
opts: the patient's right to make informed decisions about his or her own care
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. A core principle of medical ethics.
